correctness.rationale: Exact signed boundary rank 6 is proved by simplex chain exactness and reconstructed by rational Gaussian elimination. This forces at least four starting vertices on each bipartition side; one explicit eight-vertex forcing sequence proves sharpness. The 44,100 balanced candidates are all checked by both sequential and synchronous forcing, with 13,520 successes. Independent generalized-Petersen graph construction checks all 125,970 eight-vertex masks and reproduces the count. The group of order 240 is proved and its 67 orbits exactly cover the 13,520 sets.

No stronger covering optimum-set enumerator was located.

evidence: Butler–Grout–Hall explicitly determine Z(D)=8 (DOI 10.13001/1081-3810.2900, Figure 5.1 and p.11).
Their zero-diagonal, rank-twelve signed matrix gives nullity eight and, together with bipartiteness, supports a dimension-four kernel on each side.
The two independent present algorithms count all 44,100 balanced candidates and all 125,970 eight-element subsets, respectively; 13,520 success, 67 full-group orbits.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The old minimum and even the balanced cardinality constraint may be derived from earlier matrix evidence; they are credited, not the originality anchor. Exact optimum-set multiplicity and orbit distribution require additional combinatorial classification and are not entailed by Z(D)=8, the signed-matrix nullity bound, or a family-level scalar upper bound.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The Desargues graph is the incidence graph H(5,2), the bipartite double cover of the Petersen graph, and P(10,3); these are equivalent descriptions of the same object. Prior scalar Z=8 is explicitly acknowledged. A list of 13,520 optimum subsets and its 67 symmetry orbits does not follow from a scalar value or one witness. The correction could conceivably contain an unreported exact table; lack of full text is retained as risk.

evidence: The 2015 primary treatment records Z(D)=8 and examples of forcing sets, not an orbit census.
The 2020 primary treatment gives bounds for generalized Petersen graphs rather than a table of all 8-sets of P(10,3).
Relevant public research searches did not locate an existing 13,520-set or 67-orbit table; negative search alone is not claimed as proof of priority.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The exact finite object is the set of ordinary zero-forcing masks of weight 8, and the counted equivalence is full graph-automorphism equivalence, not labelled-coloring equivalence. The independent candidate census and orbit partition are provided for comparison to any future table. Full-text unavailability of the 2026 correction remains an explicit priority risk.

originality.rationale: The precise contribution is the complete optimum-set multiplicity 13,520 and 67 full-automorphism orbits. The scalar Z=8 and supporting signed-matrix rank information were previously published and are explicitly credited. Relevant exact and family primary work was compared by implication, and no inspected result supplies the entire optimum classification. Priority risk remains for the inaccessible 2026 correction or an unindexed table.

value.rationale: Optimal zero-forcing initial sets on the canonical 20-vertex Desargues graph are mathematically motivated by propagation and matrix nullity. The new exhaustive classification identifies 13,520 feasible optima and exactly 67 symmetry types, with a complete representative catalogue and two independent graph-model computations. This structural finite classification is not a scalar-value recomputation or an arbitrary unmotivated slice.
